verified_claims: Breiman (1996) Stacked Regressions, read in full from the Berkeley tech report PDF. These are confirmed: ridge results were 'better than using the least squares {ak}, but were not consistent'; the fix is non-negative least squares on cross-validated level-one data; the sum-to-one constraint is 'largely unnecessary'; Table 1 gives Housing 20.9 -> 19.0 and Ozone 23.9 -> 21.6; 'Stacking never does worse than selecting the single best predictor'; 'The more similar the predictors, the less advantage there is in stacking' (the scan reads 'tess'); 10-fold CV level-one data beat leave-one-out in simulation (the differences were small); Le Blanc & Tibshirani also found non-negativity gave the most accurate combinations. Caveat: all of these are iid experiments with randomly assigned CV folds.

Ting & Witten (1999) JAIR, arXiv 1105.5466, full text checked. Of C4.5, IB1, NB and MLR as level-1 learners, only MLR (multi-response linear regression) was suitable. The combiner should use confidences, not bare predictions. The non-negativity constraint is 'unnecessary in classification tasks' for accuracy but makes the weights easier to interpret.

Phillips, van der Laan, Lee & Gruber, arXiv 2204.06139, published in Int J Epidemiol 52(4):1276-1285 (2023), full text checked. Confirmed: larger V for smaller effective sample size (LOOCV when it is very small); clustered observations must go into the same fold as a group; parametric learners (lasso, shallow trees) for small n_eff; the ensemble SL should be entered as one candidate in a discrete SL alongside its own components.

Benkeser, Ju, Lendle & van der Laan (2018) Stat Med 37(2):249-260 exists. The abstract covers data generated sequentially, including time-series models, and says the CV-selected estimator is 'asymptotically guaranteed to perform as well as' the best candidate.

Wang, Hyndman, Li & Kang, 'Forecast combinations: an over 50-year review', IJF 39(4):1518-1547 (volume and pages confirmed via Crossref), full text checked. Confirmed: combinations that ignore correlations beat covariance-aware ones (Bates-Granger, Newbold-Granger, Winkler-Makridakis); nonlinear-combination evidence rests on 'fewer than ten time series, possibly hand-picked'; nonlinear combiners have unstable estimates and multicollinearity; rolling-origin time-series CV is recommended for stacking.

Aiolfi & Timmermann (2006) J Econometrics 135(1-2):31-53 exists. Per Wang et al. §2, it clusters forecasts with k-means on their historical performance, pools within each cluster, then estimates weights on the clusters. The clustering is by past performance, not by error correlation.

Diebold & Shin (2019) IJF 35(4):1679-1691, abstract checked on IDEAS. The 'partially-egalitarian LASSO' sets some weights to zero and shrinks the rest toward equality. Ex post, 'the vast majority of forecasters should be discarded, and the remainder should be averaged.'
Genre, Kenny, Meyler & Timmermann (2013) IJF 29(1):108-121. For GDP growth and unemployment only a few schemes beat the simple average; the evidence of improvement is stronger for inflation.
Ranjan & Gneiting (2010) JRSS B 72(1):71-91. Theorem 1: any non-trivial weighted average of distinct calibrated probability forecasts is uncalibrated. They propose the beta-transformed linear pool.

Hubáček, Šourek & Železný (2019) IJF 35:783-796, full text read, NBA 2007-2014. A model whose only input is the odds 'would have no choice but to coincide perfectly with the bookmaker'. The loss is (p̂−y)² − c·(p̂−1/o)². With the opt strategy, positive returns held for 0.4 ≤ C ≤ 0.8.

Yeung et al. arXiv 2309.14807, full text checked. Task 1 (exact scores): Berrar ratings 1.0047 vs XGBoost+Berrar ratings 1.0212. Task 2 (probabilities): CatBoost+pi-ratings best at 0.2085, σ 0.0083. It reports Tsokos et al. hierarchical RPS 0.2087 and Constantinou HBN 0.2083. Over 216,000 matches.
Hubáček, Šourek & Železný (2019) Machine Learning 108:29-47 (Crossref) was the winning 2017 Soccer Prediction Challenge entry, with test RPS 0.2063 (from the paper's own PDF).

nfelo's in-season update, read from greerreNFL/nfelo elo_shift.py, raises K by (1 + |model_error − market_error| / market_resist_factor) only when the model error exceeds the closing-market error. So nfelo absorbs past closing-line information, as GF02 said.
sklearn: StackingRegressor trains final_estimator_ on cross_val_predict output. cross_val_predict docs say 'Each sample belongs to exactly one test set'. The default cv is 5-fold KFold.

Repos: ecpolley/SuperLearner is active (push Aug 2026), DESCRIPTION says License GPL-3 and Version 2.0-40, and R/method.R has method.NNLS (normalizes to sum 1 and warns when all weights are zero) and method.CC_LS. tlverse/origami is GPL-3 and active, and R/fold_funs.R has folds_rolling_origin, folds_rolling_window, folds_rolling_origin_pooled and folds_vfold_rolling_origin_pooled with a gap argument. flennerhag/mlens is MIT, last push Nov 2023.
Wolpert (1992) Neural Networks 5(2):241-259 confirmed via Crossref.
The earlier-research attributions check out: F02 contains the 0.68 + 0.632·market collapse and the Yao/Claeskens/Smith-Wallis reviews; N12 reviews Qian et al. mAFTER (Econometrics 7(3):39, 2019).

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: The 2017 Soccer Prediction Challenge 'winners were GBMs trained on rating features: XGBoost on Berrar ratings (RPS 0.2054) and XGBoost on pi-ratings plus PageRank (0.2063)'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Wrong. Yeung et al. say Berrar's 0.2054 XGBoost result 'was obtained after the competition had concluded'; Berrar's best in-competition entry was k-NN at RPS 0.2149. Only Hubáček et al. (0.2063) won. Their winning model also used more than ratings: pi-ratings, PageRank, historical strength, form and league features. Pi-ratings alone scored 0.2067 (Hubáček MLJ 2019, Table 5).

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: 'A GBM on ratings beats weighting only slightly... The best documented gain is about 0.003 RPS' (Finding 4)
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: The 0.002-0.003 gap compares different teams' entire pipelines: a GBM against a Poisson hierarchical model and a Bayesian network, each with its own rating system. It is not a controlled comparison of a GBM against a linear or weighted combination of the same ratings, and no cited source runs that comparison. Some of the numbers mix post-competition and in-competition results. The prior that a GBM will not beat a linear stack at about 270 games a season is reasonable, but it is opinion, not evidence from these sources.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Yeung et al. show 'Putting a GBM on top of ratings can make results worse'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Only partly supported. It holds only for Task 1 (exact-score loss), where the Berrar-vs-XGBoost gap (0.0165) is smaller than Berrar's own σ of 0.0434. On the probability task, CatBoost on pi-ratings was best. No raw-ratings (non-GBM) baseline was run for probabilities.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: sklearn TimeSeriesSplit incompatibility means 'that default path is shuffled K-fold'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Wrong detail. The StackingRegressor docs say the default splitters are 'instantiated with shuffle=False' (unshuffled 5-fold KFold). The lookahead conclusion still holds, because the early blocks are predicted by base models fit on later games.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: F02 'finds that the components collapse to about 3 independent factors'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Overstated. F02 characterizes the signals as correlated transformations ('call it ~3 independent factors'). It reports no factor analysis or measured eigenstructure, so treat the number as a heuristic.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Aiolfi & Timmermann support grouping components by out-of-fold error correlation (|ρ| > 0.9)
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Misattributed. They cluster with k-means on historical forecast performance, not error correlation. The |ρ| > 0.9 family rule is the report's own design and has no source.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Exponential time-decay of combiner training data is justified because 'Claeskens warns that stale weights add bias'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Not verified. Claeskens et al. (2016), as summarized in F02, is about estimated weights being random, which adds bias and variance compared with fixed weights. 'Staleness' comes from F02's interpretation, not from the paper. Decay would need its own forward-validated justification.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Effective sample size may be 'closer to weeks (about 18 a season) than games'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: No source or measurement. Within-week residual correlation of NFL margins has not been shown to be large. Present it as an untested hypothesis to measure, not a likely fact.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Dawid (1984) JRSS A 147:278-292; van der Laan, Polley & Hubbard (2007) SAGMB 6(1)
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Not fetched in this check, because the web-search budget was exhausted and the publisher pages returned 403. Both are well-known and the bibliographic details look standard, but their specific content was not re-verified here.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: tlverse/origami folds_vfold_rolling_origin_pooled is a template for week-clustered forward folds
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Misfit. The vfold_*_pooled variants V-fold over subject ids and roll over time, but every NFL game involves two team ids. The right template is folds_rolling_origin_pooled or folds_rolling_window_pooled with time = week index and gap >= 0.
The GitHub repo's last push was Aug 2018 (stale), and the GitHub API reports no license (the license was not checked on CRAN). Idea-only reference at most.

refuted_or_unverifiable.claim: Ridge-to-equal-weights with w >= 0 via 'closed form, then an active-set pass'
refuted_or_unverifiable.problem: Taking the closed form and then clipping or running an ad hoc active-set pass does not give the constrained optimum in general. It can be solved exactly as NNLS on an augmented system: stack sqrt(λ)·I under Z and sqrt(λ)·w_eq under y−a, with the intercept centered out first. The same Lawson-Hanson routine then covers both candidates (b) and (c).

recommendations_to_drop_or_change: Fix the internal contradiction. Recommendation 1 and the family list in recommendation 2 include 'external ratings (nfelo etc.)' in the fundamentals stack, while recommendation 4 says nfelo must be kept out of stack A because it absorbs closing-line errors. Pick one: nfelo is excluded from stack A.

Make the model selection itself nested and walk-forward. Choosing among candidates (a)-(d), λ, the decay half-life, the family threshold, the correlation penalty c and the GBM hyperparameters must happen inside each forward fold, using only data before that fold. The walk-forward score must be computed on the selected-then-refit pipeline. Otherwise the reported RMSE/CLV is optimistically biased. Register every selectable knob in F06. With about 270 games a season, fix the family grouping and the λ grid a priori rather than searching them.

Do not use nfelo or nfelo-minus-opener, in either stack or as a CLV feature, until it is verified that the stored nfelo history is an as-published point-in-time snapshot rather than a recomputation with parameters tuned on the full history. This is currently open question D1; it should be a blocking precondition, not an open question.

Stack B (opener + shrunk·(A − opener)) conflicts with the owner's memory, which says the 'opener path [is] dead for this model'. It also has a much smaller sample, because openers and snapshots exist only for recent seasons. Keep it as a registered research candidate graded on CLV, not the default bet model, unless it passes the continuous out-of-sample gate.
Drop candidate (d), the GBM residual booster, from the plan. The evidence cited for it does not isolate GBM-vs-linear gains, and D5 already concedes it is undetectable at this sample size.

Replace the Aiolfi-Timmermann justification for correlation-based families with a plain design rationale. Better: define families a priori by information source (margin, play efficiency, situational/QB, external ratings) instead of a data-driven |ρ| threshold. That avoids another leak-prone and searchable step.
Change 'closed form then active-set pass' to exact NNLS on an augmented design for the ridge-to-equal candidate.

Soften Finding 4 and the soccer evidence. Remove 'winners were GBMs on Berrar ratings (0.2054)' and correct it to: Hubáček et al. won at 0.2063 using a GBM on ratings plus other features; Berrar's 0.2054 was post-competition.
Qualify 'stacking never did worse than the single best predictor' as holding in Breiman's iid simulations and tree experiments, not as a guarantee for small, time-ordered NFL samples.
Time-decay weighting should not be attributed to Claeskens. If kept, the half-life needs a forward-validated justification and a trial-registry entry.
corrected_summary:
What survives verification:
1. **Out-of-sample component forecasts are required.** Stacking needs component forecasts the combiner did not train on (Wolpert 1992; Breiman 1996, read in full).
2. **In time-ordered NFL data, those forecasts must be strictly prequential.** Each rating gets refit through week w−1, with its parameters tuned only on earlier seasons, and stored bitemporally per F05. sklearn's default StackingRegressor uses cross_val_predict with unshuffled 5-fold KFold (not shuffled, as the report says). That still lets base models fit on later games predict earlier ones, so it is lookahead.
3. **Non-negative least squares is the evidence-backed default linear combiner.** Breiman found ridge 'better... but not consistent' and non-negative LS consistently good, with sum-to-one largely unnecessary. Ting & Witten found MLR the only suitable level-1 learner, with non-negativity mainly aiding interpretability. SuperLearner's method.NNLS (GPL-3, active, v2.0-40) is a valid idea reference.
4. **Expect little from recombining similar ratings.** Breiman: 'the more similar the predictors, the less advantage'. Simple or egalitarian averages are hard to beat: Genre et al. 2013 (inflation the exception); Diebold & Shin 2019, where the ex-post optimum was to discard most forecasters and average the rest; Wang et al. 2023, where correlation-ignoring weights beat covariance-aware ones and nonlinear-combiner wins rest on fewer than ten possibly hand-picked series.
5. **Validation design.** Wang et al. recommend rolling-origin CV. Phillips et al. 2023 recommend clustered folds for dependent data and small-sample-friendly learners, and nesting the ensemble inside a discrete super learner next to its components. Benkeser et al. 2018 extend CV-based ensembles to sequential data with an asymptotic oracle guarantee.
6. **Market inputs.** A model fed only the odds coincides with the bookmaker and loses the margin (Hubáček et al. IJF 2019, NBA). Their decorrelation loss (p̂−y)² − c·(p̂−1/o)² was profitable for 0.4 ≤ C ≤ 0.8 in their data, but it is unreplicated for NFL spreads. nfelo's update uses closing-line error, so it is market-tainted.
7. **Linear pools of calibrated probabilities are uncalibrated** (Ranjan & Gneiting 2010). Combine margins, then map them through one fitted margin distribution and recalibrate.
8. **GBM-on-ratings evidence is weak and uncontrolled.** Hubáček et al. won the 2017 Soccer Challenge at RPS 0.2063 with XGBoost on ratings plus other features (pi-ratings alone 0.2067). Berrar's 0.2054 was post-competition. Yeung et al. found raw Berrar ratings beat XGBoost on the same ratings for exact scores, while CatBoost on pi-ratings was best for probabilities (σ 0.0083). No source isolates GBM against linear stacking of the same ratings, so at about 270 games a season a GBM layer is unjustified.

Recommendations that survive, for Gridiron HQ:
- **(1) Prequential component forecasts** in a bitemporal component_forecast table.
- **(2) A priori families by information source**, averaged equally within each family. The market and nfelo are excluded from the fundamentals stack.
- **(3) A small discrete super learner**, chosen by nested rolling-origin validation with week-blocked folds (origami folds_rolling_origin_pooled as the idea template, not the vfold variant). Candidates:
  - (a) equal average, as a permanent fallback;
  - (b) NNLS with intercept;
  - (c) ridge shrunk toward equal weights under w ≥ 0, solved exactly as NNLS on an augmented design.
  All selection and tuning happens inside each forward fold, and every knob is registered in F06.
- **(4) Grade fundamentals on RMSE vs margin.** Keep any opener-relative bet model as a separately registered research candidate graded on CLV. It is small-sample and in tension with the owner's note that the opener path is dead. nfelo-derived features stay blocked until the stored nfelo history is proven point-in-time.
- **(5) Implement NNLS (Lawson-Hanson) in JS or numpy.** No installs are needed.
- **(6) Set expectations.** Combination will not close most of the 14.8 vs 13.55 RMSE gap; gains must come from dissimilar information.

Unsupported or removed: the claim that the soccer 'winners' were GBMs including Berrar's 0.2054; 'shuffled' K-fold; the 3-factor finding presented as measured; correlation-based families attributed to Aiolfi-Timmermann; decay justified by Claeskens; effective sample of about 18 per season; the GBM residual candidate.
